title: Seeing whole-organ innervation
objective: Explain how whole-mount and clearing reveal innervation that sections miss.

steps.title: The whole arbor at once
steps.body: A single afferent can branch across a large territory. Thin sections chop that arbor into fragments. **[[whole-mount]]** staining and **[[tissue clearing]]** (plus 3D microscopy) let you see an ending's full shape in the intact organ — how it tiles the [[colon]] wall, where it goes, what it's near.

steps.prompt: Why prefer whole-mount/cleared tissue for mapping an afferent's endings?
options: It preserves the full 3D arbor instead of fragmenting it into sections
It images living tissue, so you can watch the endings move
It removes the need to label the afferents you want to see
It raises resolution enough to resolve single synaptic contacts
steps.explanation: Seeing the intact arbor in 3D reveals branching and territory that serial sections lose. You still need labels (markers/antibodies), and fixation is separate.

variants.setup: You want an afferent's complete ending morphology in the gut wall.
options: A single thin cryosection on a slide
A western blot of the tissue lysate
variants.reveal: Whole-mount/cleared imaging preserves the full 3D arbor that sections fragment.

steps.setup: Two studies disagree on whether one gut afferent forms multiple ending types.
steps.prompt: How could whole-organ 3D imaging help settle it?
options: By tracing single labeled afferents' complete arbors in intact tissue
By densely labeling all fibers and measuring total fluorescence
By sequencing bulk RNA from the whole dissected gut at once
By counting labeled fibers in one single thin section
steps.reveal: Following a single, sparsely-labeled afferent through intact tissue shows directly whether it makes one or several ending morphologies — a question (from the 2025 review) that fragmented sections can't resolve.

variants.prompt: To test if one afferent makes several ending types, you'd…
options: Trace single arbors in whole, cleared tissue
Label all fibers densely and measure total signal
Bulk-sequence the entire dissected gut at once
variants.explanation: Only intact 3D tracing of single cells resolves whole-arbor morphology.

sources.note: Review mapping the open questions in spinal sensory innervation of the gut.
